title: Coaching and the Freedom to Be Yourself
author: Chance Foster
summary: Chance Foster argues that coaching has bifurcated into two fundamentally different activities: human optimization (whether delivered by AI tools or in-house coaches aligned to organizational performance metrics) and transformational coaching (aimed at human becoming, uniqueness, and freedom). While optimization coaching has legitimate uses when chosen freely, the article warns that systemic deployment of optimization-oriented coaching communicates a message about which parts of a person are acceptable and which parts are not. Foster is particularly concerned about three cultural forces that push against individuality: the therapeutic model of self-understanding (which pathologizes uniqueness), increasingly alienating work, and social isolation. Transformational coaching, by contrast, stands against conformity: it sees the person's intensity, sensitivity, and unconventional thinking as individuality rather than pathology. The piece argues that transformation requires a real human relationship — not because AI tools are necessarily bad, but because human becoming happens in the specific conditions of being truly witnessed by another person.
points: The distinction between optimization coaching and transformational coaching is not one of technique but of fundamental orientation: optimization coaches toward better fit and performance within existing structures; transformation coaches toward becoming, uniqueness, and freedom.

AI-enabled 'coaching' tools deployed company-wide strip out the relationship while delivering optimization — which Foster argues is not coaching in any meaningful sense, even when it is labeled as such.

The therapeutic model has done something significant to how people understand themselves: by interpreting individuality as pathology (anxiety, attachment disorder, trauma response), it discourages people from owning the very traits that make them distinctive and generative.

Transformational coaching is 'countercultural in a good way' — it pushes against the forces of conformity (therapeutic framing, alienating work, social isolation) that move people away from independent thinking and realizing their own uniqueness.

Human transformation is not about fitting in; it is about creating, growing, and becoming. Coaching that does not create the conditions for transformation — even when it improves performance — misses the most important thing it could be doing.
quotes: The popularity of coaching reflects its value. The 'scaling,' has split coaching into two different things at the extremes. On one end, AI-enabled 'coaching' tools now offer employees company-wide something like human optimization — stripping out the relationship and honing in on what to do and how to do it.

Here is the current state of coaching: it spans the space between human workforce optimization (with or without human intervention) and genuine human transformation. Which is better for people is the one that gives them more power and more choice; that is the latter — transformational coaching in relationship with real humans.

The last fifty years have seen psychotherapy become the dominant socio-emotional framework for self-understanding in the Western world. When we locate the source of our struggles primarily in our stories of distress and difference, we frame what might otherwise be individuality — intensity, sensitivity, unconventional thinking — as pathology.

Transformational coaching is countercultural in a good way. Our world trains compliance, submission, and passivity from a young age, moving us away from independent thinking and realizing our own uniqueness.

Transformational coaching stands in contrast to three powerful social forces that push us toward conformity: the ubiquity of the therapeutic model of who we are, work that is increasingly alienating, and a social reality that leaves us isolated.
Human transformation is not about fitting in. It is about creating, growing, and becoming. It is good for society to grow individuals, but hard at the same time.
